promptOriginal: Turn a vague healthcare AI governance idea into a precise, impressive visual: a calm operations dashboard showing model ownership, review queues, exception paths, and human approval gates.
subject: scene: A healthcare AI governance operations dashboard in active monitoring mode; environment: A clean enterprise control-room style interface with subtle healthcare context, presented as a polished product-visual rather than a literal hospital setting; keyElements: model ownership panel listing named AI systems, owners, status, and accountability indicators; review queue panel showing pending policy reviews, triage priority, and aging items; exception path flow showing flagged cases branching into escalation lanes; human approval gates with clearly marked sign-off checkpoints before deployment or release; audit timeline or compliance rail indicating recent reviews and approvals; subtle healthcare cues such as shield icons, care-related labels, or clinical-quality color semantics without showing patients or charts tied to real individuals; contentBoundaries: No patient faces; No biometric scans; No medical procedures; No personally identifiable information
style: visualMode: high-fidelity product illustration blended with premium dashboard UI design; mood: calm, trustworthy, precise, impressive; finish: clean glass-and-matte surfaces, crisp typography, subtle depth, restrained glow accents; realism: semi-realistic interface visualization rather than photorealistic hardware photography; lighting: soft neutral studio lighting with gentle screen illumination; detailLevel: high
composition: framing: wide landscape composition; cameraAngle: straight-on with a slight elevated perspective for readability; layout: central governance dashboard as the focal point, with ownership and queue panels balanced on the sides, and exception/approval flow elements clearly connected across the canvas; visualHierarchy: primary focus on governance overview; secondary focus on review queues and ownership accountability; tertiary focus on exception routing and human approval checkpoints; density: information-rich but uncluttered, with deliberate spacing and obvious grouping
palette: blues and teals for trust and governance, warm amber accents only for exceptions or approvals, high readability with restrained saturation
negativeConstraints: Do not depict patients, doctors, or identifiable human faces as the main subject
Do not include gore, surgery, illness imagery, or emergency scenes
Do not show real brand logos, hospital names, or vendor trademarks
Do not include visible personal data, medical records, or realistic patient charts
Do not make the interface chaotic, neon-heavy, cyberpunk, or alarmist
Do not use dark horror aesthetics, red-dominant warning palettes, or crisis-room tension
Do not render the dashboard as a generic finance terminal
Do not imply autonomous medical decision-making without human review
safetyProfile: category: benign enterprise healthcare governance visualization; riskLevel: low; allowedContent: abstract healthcare operations context; governance workflows; compliance and approval interfaces; non-identifying UI labels and metrics; disallowedContent: patient-specific data; diagnostic claims; medical treatment depiction; fear-inducing failure scenarios; notes: The image should communicate oversight, accountability, and human control in a healthcare-adjacent setting without showing sensitive clinical content.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Image is delivered in a 1536x1024 landscape format.
The visual contains clearly distinguishable sections for model ownership, review queues, exception paths, and human approval gates.
No patient identities, faces, personal records, or real-world branded healthcare entities are visible.
The composition reads immediately as a governance or oversight dashboard rather than a clinical treatment scene or a finance console.
The image feels calm, trustworthy, and premium, with strong visual hierarchy and low visual noise.
Healthcare context is present but subtle, reinforcing safety and accountability without relying on cliché hospital imagery.
Human approval checkpoints are visually legible as meaningful control gates within the workflow rather than decorative icons.
